title: Squares, Anchors, Fonts, Spirals & Sanitizers
description: A polar-math boot spiral, self-sizing anchor-size() panels, the real Local Font Access API, a raw-WebGL square lens, and the new Sanitizer API cleaning hostile paste live.

drops.title: Spiral Boot
drops.description: A tile grid converges into place via angle-increasing/radius-shrinking polar math, staggered per-tile for a trailing spiral effect.
drops.concept: Reimplements the preloader technique from a recent portfolio case study: rather than animating along a path, each element stores its own polar angle and radius, which are tweened independently and converted to x/y every frame. Accelerating the shared angle while collapsing the radii produces a spiral gather; reversing it produces a scatter. A 0.09s per-tile stagger creates the trailing motion.
drops.source: Inspired by Matt Stone's Goodgrowth portfolio (via a Codrops case study)

interaction.mouse: Click any tile for an independent mini spiral-snap pulse
interaction.click: Spiral In / Spiral Out buttons replay the full sequence
interaction.touch: Tap tiles the same as click

drops.title: Anchor-Size Spec Panel
drops.description: A comparison drawer whose height is set purely in CSS with anchor-size(height) — it always matches the card that opened it, live, with no JS measuring.
drops.concept: CSS anchor positioning shipped position-anchor and anchor() for placement, but anchor-size() goes further: it lets a positioned element's own sizing properties read a live dimension off its anchor. Here a product spec panel is pinned beside whichever card was clicked and its height literally is anchor-size(height) — drag the card's resize handle and the panel resyncs instantly with zero ResizeObserver.

interaction.mouse: Click a card to open its matched-height spec panel
interaction.click: Drag the ⠿ handle to resize a card and watch the panel follow
interaction.touch: Tap to open, drag handle to resize

drops.title: System Font Explorer
drops.description: Grants the real Local Font Access API and lists every font installed on your machine, each rendering your own live preview text.
drops.concept: window.queryLocalFonts() is a genuine, permissioned browser API that enumerates locally installed font families — no font files are shipped by the page and nothing is uploaded anywhere. This drop requests access, lists every family found, and lets you type custom preview text, filter by name, and apply any font to a hero showcase. Unsupported browsers get a graceful generic font-stack fallback instead of an error.

interaction.mouse: Click 'Access Local Fonts' to grant permission and list your fonts
interaction.click: Click any font row to apply it to the hero showcase
interaction.touch: Tap to grant access and select fonts

drops.title: Shader Square Lens
drops.description: A raw-WebGL fragment shader composites grayscale and color images through a mouse-following square mask, with lens distortion and RGB shift inside.
drops.concept: Two procedurally generated textures — one full color, one its grayscale twin — are drawn in a single fragment shader pass. A step-function mask carves out a square around the cursor; inside it, a CC-lens-style radial scale bulges the image outward and a radial RGB channel shift intensifies toward the edges, while outside the square the grayscale field ripples with a sine wave plus per-pixel noise. Built in raw WebGL (no Three.js) to stay dependency-free.
drops.source: Inspired by Tomoyuki Nakata's Codrops tutorial

interaction.mouse: Move the cursor to drag the lens across the field
interaction.click: Switch pattern presets and tune distortion in the debug panel
interaction.touch: Drag a finger to move the lens

drops.title: Safe Paste
drops.description: Type or paste hostile HTML and watch the Sanitizer API strip it live, with an itemized list of exactly what got removed.
drops.concept: The new browser-native Sanitizer API (Element.setHTML with a default-safe Sanitizer) strips script tags, event-handler attributes, and unsafe javascript: URLs before content ever touches the DOM. This component never renders the raw input — only an escaped text view plus the sanitized, safe-to-display result — and independently inspects the parsed (inert) DOM tree to report exactly which tags and attributes were stripped, with a matching allowlist-based fallback for browsers without native support yet.
drops.source: Sanitizer API, via Chrome for Developers

interaction.mouse: Click a preset or type your own HTML in the raw pane
interaction.click: Presets demonstrate script, onerror, and javascript: URL attacks plus clean formatting
